items.title: Reduce service account token exposure
items.rationale: Mounted service account tokens expand blast radius when a pod is compromised and should be disabled unless the workload truly needs Kubernetes API access.
actions: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false for workloads that do not need the API.
Use a dedicated least-privilege service account when API access is required.
Keep token mounts read-only and review RBAC bindings.

items.title: Mount the root filesystem read-only
items.rationale: Writable root filesystems make persistence and tampering easier after compromise.
actions: Move writable paths to explicit emptyDir or persistent volumes.
Validate startup scripts and temp directories still work after the change.
items.snippet:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: REPLACE_ME
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: target-kata,role=target
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: REPLACE_ME
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          runAsGroup: 10001
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault
items.risk_note: Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem can break workloads that write under /tmp, /var, /etc, or application paths.

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1

      app: target-kata,role=target
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  ingress: []
  egress:
  - to:

    - protocol: TCP

kind: ServiceAccount

  name: sandbox-sa
  namespace: sandbox-kata
automountServiceAccountToken: false
templates.kyverno_policy:
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: sandbox-restricted
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  rules:
  - name: require-restricted-security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: Enforce restricted securityContext for sandbox workloads.
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              seccompProfile:
                type: RuntimeDefault
templates.gatekeeper_template:
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRequiredSandboxSecurity
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "Sandbox pods must set readOnlyRootFilesystem=true"
      }

ai_advisor.executive_summary: Two high-severity issues: a mounted service account token and a writable root filesystem. Both increase risk if an attacker compromises the pod. Automated fixes were withheld due to potential breakage; operator review required.
ai_advisor.remediation_overview: Confirm application needs before changing. For the service account token, disable automount if the pod does not call the Kubernetes API. For rootfs, identify writable paths and move them to explicit writable volumes (emptyDir) then enable readOnlyRootFilesystem.

prioritized_groups.title: Credentials and API access
prioritized_groups.rationale: Service account token exposure allows lateral movement and cluster API misuse; high blast radius and immediate impact.

prioritized_groups.title: Filesystem immutability
prioritized_groups.rationale: Writable root filesystem enables persistence for an attacker and tampering with code/config; requires compatibility checks before enforcing.

item_advice.explanation: Pod currently mounts a service account token, exposing credentials to processes in the container.
item_advice.operator_impact: Disabling automount breaks any in-pod code that calls the Kubernetes API using the token.
item_advice.validation_advice: Search container logs and code for in-cluster API calls; test disabling automount in a staging clone of the deployment.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Prevent privileged credentials first to reduce attacker capability quickly.

item_advice.explanation: Root filesystem is writable, allowing attackers to modify binaries, config, or persist artifacts.
item_advice.operator_impact: Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem will break paths the app must write to; requires moving those paths to writable volumes.
item_advice.validation_advice: Run the container with readOnlyRootFilesystem in staging; verify writes succeed to designated writable mounts (e.g., workspace, /tmp mapped to emptyDir).
item_advice.ordering_reason: After credentials are addressed, enforce filesystem immutability to limit post-exploit persistence.

ai_advisor.guided_operator_message: Review API usage and writable paths in this deployment; test fixes in staging before rolling to production.
warnings: Do not enable fixes in-place without compatibility testing; both fixes can break the workload.

next_steps: Audit pods for in-cluster Kubernetes API calls (tokens usage).
If no API use, patch Deployment to set automountServiceAccountToken: false in pod spec.
Identify application writable paths; move them to explicit volumes or emptyDir mounts.
Test enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem in a staging replica.
Deploy changes to production only after successful staging validation.
